IMD Issues Red Alert for Meghalaya, Arunachal; Heavy Rain Likely in Parts of Assam
First Published: 4th August, 2026 14:03 IST
According to IMD, orange and red alerts have been issued for East Khasi Hills, West Jaintia Hills, East Jaintia Hills districts, Meghalaya.
The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued a warning of extremely heavy rainfall accompanied by thunderstorms across parts of Meghalaya and Arunachal Pradesh over the next three to four days.
The weather department has warned that the overall weather conditions could also affect several districts in Assam, including Cachar, Dima Hasao, West Karbi Anglong, Biswanath, Lakhimpur, Dhemaji and Tinsukia, advising residents to remain vigilant.
According to the IMD, orange and red alerts have been issued for East Khasi Hills, West Jaintia Hills and East Jaintia Hills districts of Meghalaya, where thunderstorms with lightning and extremely heavy rainfall are expected. Similar weather conditions are forecast for Papumpare, Kurung Kumey, East Kameng, East Siang, Lohit and Changlang districts of Arunachal Pradesh. The department warned that these may also have an impact on adjoining districts of Assam.
The IMD has additionally placed several Nagaland districts bordering Assam under a yellow alert. The weather conditions in these areas are likely to affect Assam’s Charaideo, Sivasagar, Jorhat and Golaghat districts.
For Kamrup Metro, including Guwahati, the IMD has forecast heavy rainfall that could worsen waterlogging, urban flooding and flash flood situations. The department also warned of slower vehicular movement and an increased risk of landslides in vulnerable areas.
The warning comes after heavy overnight rainfall lashed Guwahati on Monday, leaving several parts of the city inundated and causing severe waterlogging that disrupted traffic and affected normal life.
